mechanism: Opposition Solve: Instead of asking "how do I achieve X?", ask "how would I guarantee failure at X?" or "how would I achieve NOT-X?". List answers. Invert each answer to get candidate {{solution}}s for original {{problem}}. Often reveals blind spots. It applies {{reframe}} by negating the goal {{state}}, solving for failure to identify necessary conditions for success.
failure_modes: False dichotomy: the opposite of failure is taken for success, when it may only be mediocrity.
Necessary but not sufficient: avoiding every enumerated failure does not produce the goal, only the conditions it needs.
invariants: Inversion is logical negation, not merely the opposite.
Every enumerated failure path is inverted, not just the first.
Double negation returns the original: Invert(Invert(X)) implies X.
